answer: Necessary to optimize. The best plan: wrap the if-else block (including Node.from and the else branch) in a try-catch that catches NumberFormatException from Node.from. In the catch block, create the default node using getLocalhostName and defaultPort. This uses only one try-catch structure and handles the most likely recoverable runtime exception.
remark: Caught NumberFormatException thrown by Node.from to fall back to default node creation using getLocalhostName and defaultPort.
analysis: The code attempts to get a current node by first obtaining KylinConfig from environment, then reading a streaming node string. If the string is not null, it parses it via Node.from; otherwise, it creates a new Node using local hostname and default port. After that, it sets properties from streaming node properties and returns. Various runtime exceptions may be thrown: getInstanceFromEnv can throw IllegalStateException, RuntimeException, SecurityException, KylinConfigCannotInitException; getStreamingNode can throw SecurityException, IllegalArgumentException, NullPointerException; Node.from can throw NumberFormatException; getLocalhostName can throw UnknownHostException; getStreamingNodeProperties can throw IllegalStateException. Among these, NumberFormatException from Node.from is recoverable: if the config string is malformed, the method can fall back to the default node creation (same as when configNodeStr is null). The other exceptions indicate serious configuration or environment issues and should propagate to the caller. Therefore, optimization is needed to catch NumberFormatException and handle gracefully.
